target: Mi preoccupavo troppo per tutto.
english: I used to worry too much about everything.
tip: Imperfetto: mi preoccupavo (preoccuparsi) for habitual past.

target: Portava sempre gli occhiali da sole.
english: She always wore sunglasses.
tip: Habits in the past: 'Ogni estate andavamo al mare' = Every summer we used to go to the beach. 'Ogni' signals imperfetto.

target: Stavano parlando di te proprio adesso.
english: They were just talking about you.
tip: Imperfetto progressivo: stavano + gerundio for action in progress.

target: Avevo vent'anni quando mi sono sposato.
english: I was twenty when I got married.
tip: Polite requests with imperfetto: 'Cercavo il signor Rossi' = I was looking for Mr. Rossi (implies: is he available?).

target: Costava molto meno dieci anni fa.
english: It cost much less ten years ago.
tip: 'C'era una volta...' = Once upon a time... Every Italian fairy tale starts with imperfetto. It sets the scene.

target: Insegnava matematica al liceo.
english: She taught math at high school.
tip: Imperfetto for interrupted actions: 'Dormivo quando è suonato il telefono' = I was sleeping when the phone rang.

target: Ci divertivamo molto d'estate.
english: We had a lot of fun in summer.
tip: Imperfetto: ci divertivamo (divertirsi) for habitual past.

target: Viaggiavamo ogni estate in Sardegna.
english: We traveled to Sardinia every summer.
tip: Physical descriptions in the past use imperfetto: 'Aveva i capelli biondi' = She had blond hair. It's a state, not an event.

target: Faceva sempre scherzi ai colleghi.
english: He always played pranks on his colleagues.
tip: Italian songs and poems use imperfetto for nostalgic, dreamy effect. It's the tense of memory and longing.

target: Guadagnavo poco ma ero contento.
english: I earned little but I was happy.
tip: Imperfetto: guadagnavo + ero for two past states.

target: Giocavano a pallone nel cortile.
english: They used to play ball in the courtyard.
tip: 'Sapevo' (I knew) vs 'Ho saputo' (I found out). Same verb, different past tense = different meaning!

target: Raccoglievamo le fragole nel campo.
english: We used to pick strawberries in the field.
tip: 'Da bambino/a' + imperfetto = When I was a child, I used to... 'Da bambino, giocavo sempre fuori.'

target: Suonavo la chitarra da ragazzo.
english: I used to play guitar as a teenager.
tip: Italian cinema dialogue is full of imperfetto for flashback scenes. Understanding it unlocks Italian films!

target: Ve lo ripeto un'altra volta.
english: I'm telling you again.
tip: Direct object pronouns (lo, la, li, le) go before the conjugated verb: "Lo vedo" (I see him/it).

target: Le vacanze passavano troppo in fretta.
english: The holidays went by too fast.
tip: Descriptions of places: 'La casa era grande e aveva un giardino' = The house was big and had a garden. All imperfetto.

target: Preferivo restare a casa il sabato.
english: I preferred to stay home on Saturdays.
tip: Italian uses imperfetto where English uses simple past for states: 'Era buono' = It was good (tasting something).

target: Il nonno mi portava a pescare.
english: Grandpa used to take me fishing.
tip: 'Non c'era nessuno' = There was nobody. Imperfetto for describing absence/emptiness in the past.

target: Amava il profumo dei fiori d'arancio.
english: She loved the scent of orange blossoms.
tip: In indirect speech, present becomes imperfetto: 'Dice: sono stanco' → 'Ha detto che era stanco' (He said he was tired).

target: Avevamo un cane che si chiamava Lucky.
english: We had a dog named Lucky.
tip: Ongoing location: 'Dove eri?' = Where were you? 'Ero a casa' = I was at home. Being somewhere = imperfetto.

target: È possibile che Marco abbia già finito.
english: It's possible Marco has already finished.
tip: Common irregular subjunctive forms: sia (essere), abbia (avere), faccia (fare), vada (andare), stia (stare).

target: Quando è arrivata la polizia, il ladro scappava.
english: When the police arrived, the thief was fleeing.
tip: Passato prossimo (è arrivata) for event + imperfetto (scappava) for ongoing action.

target: Guardavamo i cartoni animati il sabato.
english: We watched cartoons on Saturdays.
tip: 'Dovevo' (I had to/was supposed to) in imperfetto often implies the action didn't happen: unfulfilled obligation.

target: Grazie per il tuo aiuto.
english: Thank you for your help.
tip: 'Di' expresses origin, possession, and material: 'Sono di Roma', 'il libro di Marco', 'un tavolo di legno'.

target: Mi sveglio e faccio colazione.
english: I wake up and have breakfast.
tip: Reflexive verbs use reflexive pronouns (mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si) before the conjugated verb: "Mi sveglio" (I wake up).

target: Abita da solo da tre anni.
english: He's been living alone for three years.
tip: "Da" = from/since/at someone's place. "Da tre anni" (for three years), "dal dottore" (at the doctor's).

target: Quando ero piccola, avevo un gatto.
english: When I was little, I had a cat.
tip: Passato prossimo for completed events, imperfetto for background: 'Pioveva quando sono uscito' = It was raining when I left.

target: Quando siamo usciti, faceva già buio.
english: When we went out, it was already dark.
tip: Passato prossimo (siamo usciti) for event + imperfetto (faceva) for weather.

target: Voglio che i bambini mangino la verdura.
english: I want the children to eat vegetables.
tip: "Volere che" + congiuntivo: expressing a wish about someone else's action. The subjunctive is mandatory.

target: Bisogna che io faccia una telefonata urgente.
english: I must make an urgent phone call.
tip: The subjunctive form appears after "che" – triggered by the main clause expressing opinion, wish, doubt, or necessity.

target: Quando l'ho incontrata, portava un vestito rosso.
english: When I met her, she was wearing a red dress.
tip: Passato prossimo (l'ho incontrata) for event + imperfetto (portava) for description.

target: Sembra che il tempo cambi ogni cinque minuti.
english: It seems the weather changes every five minutes.
tip: Verbs of opinion, hope, doubt, or perception + "che" require the subjunctive mood.

target: Spero che il dottore mi dia buone notizie.
english: I hope the doctor gives me good news.
tip: "Dare" in the subjunctive: dia, dia, dia, diamo, diate, diano.

target: Bisogna che il ristorante migliori il servizio ai tavoli.
english: The restaurant must improve its table service.
tip: `È necessario che`, `bisogna che`, `è importante che` → next verb in congiuntivo. The trigger phrase is real, the action is hypothetical.

target: Deve lavarsi le mani.
english: He needs to wash his hands.
tip: Italian object pronouns go before the verb: 'lo vedo' (I see him/it), 'gli parlo' (I talk to him). They attach to infinitives: 'vederlo'.

target: Lui studiava mentre io dormivo.
english: He studied while I slept.
tip: 'Lui' = he (subject). The verb ending (-a for third person -are, -e for -ere/-ire) already shows the person.

target: Quando siamo arrivati, pioveva forte.
english: When we arrived, it was raining hard.
tip: Passato prossimo (siamo arrivati) for completed arrival + imperfetto (pioveva) for weather backdrop.

target: Si è sentita male al concerto.
english: She felt sick at the concert.
tip: Reflexive pronouns go before the verb: 'Mi alzo alle sette' = I get up at seven.

target: Ho comprato un libro per mia madre.
english: I bought a book for my mother.
tip: 'Da' before a person means 'at/to their place': 'Vado dal dottore' = I'm going to the doctor's.

target: Chiunque parli italiano sa quanto sia bello.
english: Whoever speaks Italian knows how beautiful it is.
tip: Indefinite pronouns/adjectives (qualunque, chiunque, ovunque) take the subjunctive in formal usage.

target: Stavo leggendo e d'improvviso è caduta la luce.
english: I was reading and suddenly the power went out.
tip: Imperfetto progressivo (stavo leggendo) for background + passato prossimo (è caduta) for sudden event.

target: Mi chiami domani?
english: Will you call me tomorrow?
tip: Direct object pronouns go before the conjugated verb: 'Lo vedo' = I see him/it.

target: La conosco da anni.
english: I've known her for years.
tip: Pronoun + verb is glued tight: `non lo conosco` (I don't know him). The pronoun never floats free.

target: Fallo adesso, non domani.
english: Do it now, not tomorrow.
tip: "Fallo" = fa' + lo – pronoun attaches to shortened form.

target: Ci siamo incontrati per caso.
english: We met by chance.
tip: `ci` = 'there' (replacing a place). `Vai al cinema? Sì, ci vado` (Yes, I go there). Saves repeating the location.

target: Si è arrabbiato per la multa.
english: He got angry about the fine.
tip: Many daily routines are reflexive in Italian: 'svegliarsi' (to wake up), 'vestirsi' (to get dressed), 'lavarsi' (to wash).

target: Potrebbe spiegarlo di nuovo, per favore?
english: Could you explain that again, please?
tip: "Potrebbe" – formal conditional of potere for polite questions.

target: Benché faccia freddo, usciamo lo stesso.
english: Although it's cold, we're going out anyway.
tip: "Benché" + subjunctive: faccia, not fa.

target: Prendine un altro, questo è rotto.
english: Take another one, this one is broken.
tip: "Prendine" = prendi + ne – partitive pronoun on imperative.

target: Da noi si cena alle otto.
english: At our place we have dinner at eight.
tip: Preposition "a" contracts with articles: a+il=al, a+lo=allo, a+la=alla, a+i=ai, a+gli=agli, a+le=alle.

target: Credo che domani faccia bel tempo.
english: I believe the weather will be nice tomorrow.
tip: `Credo che sia` not `credo che è` – opinion verbs trigger congiuntivo. The endings: -are → -i/-i/-i/-iamo/-iate/-ino. -ere/-ire → -a/-a/-a/-iamo/-iate/-ano.

target: Per colpa del traffico sono in ritardo.
english: Because of the traffic I'm late.
tip: Preposition "di" contracts with articles: di+il=del, di+lo=dello, di+la=della, di+i=dei, di+gli=degli, di+le=delle.

target: La casa in cui vivo è piccola.
english: The house I live in is small.
tip: 'In cui' is used for 'in which' in relative clauses.

target: Da allora non ci siamo più parlati.
english: Since then we haven't spoken to each other.
tip: `ci` also gets glued to other constructions: `ci sono` (there is), `ci credo` (I believe in it). It's the small word doing a lot of work.

target: Glielo dico subito.
english: I'll tell him right away.
tip: Combined pronouns: indirect + direct. "Me lo" = it to me, "glielo" = it to him/her. Indirect comes first.

target: Mi ha detto la verità.
english: He told me the truth.
tip: Indirect object pronouns (mi, ti, gli, le, ci, vi, gli) go before the verb: "Gli ho detto" (I told him).

target: È necessario che tu venga domani.
english: It's necessary that you come tomorrow.
tip: "È necessario che" + subjunctive: venga, not vieni.

target: Nonostante faccia caldo, preferisco il tè caldo.
english: Even though it's hot, I prefer hot tea.
tip: Concessive conjunctions (sebbene, benché, malgrado, nonostante) always require the subjunctive mood.

target: Vorremmo prenotare due posti per lo spettacolo.
english: We'd like to book two seats for the show.
tip: Volere in condizionale (vorrei = I would like). Very common for polite requests.

target: È meglio che tu non beva troppo caffè.
english: It's better that you don't drink too much coffee.
tip: "Bere" in the subjunctive: beva, beva, beva, beviamo, beviate, bevano.

target: Presteresti dei soldi a un amico in difficoltà?
english: Would you lend money to a friend in need?
tip: Condizionale presente: infinitive stem + -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero. Expresses wishes and polite requests.
